subject: Commercial model and lead registration — CloudForge reseller/referral proposal
messages:

Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@maverick.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Intro — CloudForge reseller/referral commercial proposal

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for taking time to chat today. As discussed, CloudForge is exploring a two-track partnership with Redwood: 1) referral fees for direct introductions to our enterprise accounts, and 2) a reseller option where CloudForge can white-label and bundle Redwood services for our ISV customers.

Attached is a short term sheet that sketches commissions and lead registration mechanics. High level: 15% on referral ARR (year 1), 10% on reseller-sourced bookings (gross before discounts), 12-month lead registration window. We're flexible on payment cadence.

Can you review and share Redwood's preferred commercial model and any must-have contract terms from your side (payment timing, clawbacks, audit rights, exclusivity)? We have a product integration roadmap that could be co-marketed — happy to include marketing credits in the final package.

Attachment: CloudForge_Redwood_Referral_Termsheet.pdf (1 page)

Best,
Anika Rao
Head of Partnerships, CloudForge
partners@cloudforge.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro — CloudForge reseller/referral commercial proposal

Anika — thanks for the term sheet and the great conversation. High level, Redwood is supportive of both tracks. A few initial positions from commercial: 

- Referral (direct intro): 18% of first-year ARR paid on a net-45 basis after invoice collection; 12-month registration window from first submitted qualified lead; commissions pay only on net new logos (no renewals).
- Reseller: 12% margin on gross billings with quarterly settlement; Redwood will provide reseller pricing matrix.
- Lead registration: CloudForge to submit leads through partner portal (we'll create an intake form); first-touch documentation required to qualify.
- Chargebacks: 6-month clawback window if customer cancels within the first 6 months.
- Co-marketing: Redwood will contribute $10k in joint-marketing credits on first-year deals > $100k ARR.

I'm looping in Dylan (SE) and Lauren (Channel) to confirm technical and GTM points. Please let us know two examples of target accounts and we'll run a quick overlap check. If this looks directionally right, I'll pull in Marcus from Legal to draft a short MOU/redline.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Vanessa / team — quick legal heads-up before we send a formal MOU. Key redline items we should consider including in the draft: 

- Definitions: "Qualified Lead" should be tightly defined (company name, contact, pain, budget range, consent to introduction).
- Commission payments: Redwood prefers net-60 for first payments with quarterly reconciliation; can accept net-45 on a case-by-case basis.
- Clawback: 6-month clawback is ok; propose pro-rata return if partial usage.
- Audit & records: Redwood needs standard audit rights for 24 months for commission verification (sample-based).
- Exclusivity: no exclusivity for either party — add explicit non-exclusivity clause.
- IP & branding: reseller may not white-label product in a way that obscures Redwood attribution; allow co-branding but retain trademark usage rights.

Attaching a short redline template I usually use for partner MOU drafts. If commercial is good with net-60 we can draft; otherwise call me and we'll decide.

Attachment: CloudForge_Redwood_Agree_Track_2025-11_redline.docx

—Marcus

Thanks Marcus and Vanessa — appreciate the clear notes. A few counterpoints from CloudForge: 

- Commission split: we'd prefer 18% on direct referral (we're bringing the lead and likely to influence SKU mix), 12% on reseller-sourced bookings. Can we meet commercial halfway: Redwood net-45 for referral payments and quarterly for reseller settlements?
- Lead registration window: Can we extend lookback to 12 months (we understand you asked for 12 months already — confirming), and make "first-touch documentation" lightweight: email thread + partner intake form should be sufficient for qualification.
- Co-sell cadence: we prefer optional monthly check-ins instead of mandated co-sell meetings in the MOU.

I've attached our redline with small language edits and a suggested reporting cadence. We're ready to move quickly if legal can land a short MOU with these points.

Attachment: CloudForge_Redwood_Agree_Track_2025-11_redline.docx (CloudForge edits)

Anika — thanks, this is helpful and performant. Quick summary of what Redwood is willing to put in the MOU based on your redline and Marcus' items: 

1) Referral track (direct intro): 18% of first-year ARR, paid net-45 after Redwood collects invoice; 12-month registration lookback; 6-month clawback.
2) Reseller track: 12% of gross billings, settled quarterly; reseller to use Redwood pricing matrix and co-brand per trademark guidelines.
3) Lead registration: CloudForge submits via partner intake (we will provision partner portal access) — email thread + intake form acceptable for qualification.
4) Audit & payment: Audit rights for 24 months (sample-based); Redwood to provide quarterly commission statements; commissions subject to standard deduction for refunds/chargebacks within 6 months.
5) No exclusivity, standard IP protections, and mutual non-disparagement language.

Next steps: Marcus will update the redline and I'll circulate the MOU. If CloudForge approves the next draft, we'll execute via DocuSign (link below) and schedule a kickoff call (target: week of 11/24) with Dylan and Lauren for the GTM plan.
